methodological_rigor.justification: The study is a prospective single-arm, multicenter phase II pilot in 30 infants with KMT2A-r CD19+ B-ALL with efficacy compared to 214 selected historical Interfant-06 controls and a matched Interfant-06 subset, with DFS/OS, cumulative incidence of relapse, and pharmacokinetic analyses (Css and CL). The historical control comparison is a recognized limitation acknowledged by the authors given ethical prohibitions against a randomized arm in this ultra-rare high-risk population. Sample size is small (n=30), AE classification differs from the historical cohort preventing direct infection comparisons, and the CL covariate analysis is underpowered. Statistical methods (Kaplan-Meier, cumulative incidence, weighted KM for matched comparison per Galimberti et al) are appropriate but basic.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Infant KMT2A-r ALL has historically poor survival (~44% 4-year DFS on Interfant-06). A 4-year DFS of 83.3% and OS of 93.3% with a single postinduction blinatumomab course represents a dramatic absolute improvement (~40 percentage points) that, if confirmed, would be practice-changing in this rare high-risk population. PK data support not adjusting dosing for infants. FDA approval from 1 month of age is referenced. Oxford LoE 2b as an individual single-arm interventional cohort vs historical controls.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT is the applicable standard for this interventional single-arm pilot study and key elements are present: enrollment, interventions, endpoints, follow-up, event definitions, and Kaplan-Meier analyses. However, many details (patient characteristics table, AE table, CL covariates, statistical analysis details, protocol) are delegated to the Data Supplement, and the manuscript is compact. No explicit CONSORT checklist reference, and the trial registration identifier for the primary study is referenced only implicitly via ref 5. No data or code sharing beyond supplementary material.

novelty_literature.justification: This is the long-term follow-up of the first prospective evaluation of frontline blinatumomab in infant KMT2A-r ALL (short-term results published in ref 5, NEJM 2023). The extension to 4-year DFS/OS, detailed infection profiling by phase, and first dedicated PK analysis in infants fills a documented gap. Related work (COG AALL1731 in older children) exists, so the regimen concept is not wholly novel, but the infant population and durability data are new.

writing_presentation.justification: The brief report is clear and well organized with a focused narrative. Figures 1 and 2 communicate survival comparisons and infection profiles effectively, and Table 1 provides cross-generational PK context. Limitations are candidly stated. The concise format is appropriate for a rapid-communication style long-term follow-up, though some reliance on the supplement.

key_strengths: Striking durable efficacy in infant KMT2A-r ALL: 4-year DFS 83.3% vs 44.0% historical, OS 93.3% vs 60.2%
No infection-related deaths postinduction vs 4% historical Interfant-06 mortality
First dedicated blinatumomab pharmacokinetic data in infants showing equivalence to older children
Multicenter enrollment (12 sites in Europe and Australia) of an ultra-rare high-risk population
Consistency with matched Interfant-06 controls and COG AALL1731 findings
key_concerns: Single-arm design with historical-control comparison; no randomization feasible in this population
Small sample size (n=30) limits subgroup and covariate analyses
Different AE classification systems preclude direct infection-toxicity comparison
Selection of Interfant-06 controls could introduce bias despite matching
CONSORT checklist not explicitly cited; limited data/code sharing
chief_reviewer.rationale: Small but highly impactful long-term follow-up demonstrating durable benefit of blinatumomab in infant KMT2A-r ALL; worthy of tier-1 placement (e.g., major hematology/oncology journal) after minor revisions pending confirmatory trials.
